newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: No end in sight to Colombia port strike.
newsitem.headline: No end in sight to Colombia port strike.

text.p: A crippling dock workers' strike at Colombia's main Pacific coast port headed into the weekend with no immediate end in sight, a cargo handling operator said Friday.

More than 160,000 60-kg bags of coffee destined for export and all the country's sugar exports have been paralyzed by the three-day-old stoppage at the port of Buenaventura. About 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports are shipped through the port.

Talks are likely to be scheduled late Friday night or over the weekend and center on a simplified list of demands presented by dockers' leaders to all sides in the dispute Friday, said Marco Cruz, head of private cargo operator Asemar SA.
"It's impossible to say when the strike will end because the latest negotiations have not even started," Cruz told Reuters.
Workers' representatives, cargo operators and ship owners reached a deal in principle to end the strike Thursday but dockers' rejected the agreement later in a general assembly.

The two dock workers' unions are calling for an increase in wages and additional sickness, injury and social security benefits. Thursday's accord collapsed when operators and ship owners granted an overall wage increase but turned down demands for an extra 22 percent to cover benefits.
The port of Buenaventura handles about 25,000 tons of cargo a day and is estimated to be losing about $500,000 for every day of the strike.
The port authority, the town mayor and the leaders of two national labor federations, to which the dock workers' unions ae affiliated, are trying to mediate the strike talks.
